description:
AN ACCOUNT WITH NOTHING LEFT TO SPEND DOES NOT SAY SO ON THE LIVE SURFACES. Reported by an operator 2026-09-15: a tasklist stopped because the provider account was out of usage, and neither `chief ps` nor `chief monitor` said that was what happened.

WHAT ALREADY WORKS, and is not to be rebuilt. A Claude usage limit is detected (`_is_rate_limit`), the scheduler waits the window out and re-dispatches, the coarse state is `rate-limited`, and `limit_note()` (engine/monitor.sh:551) renders a genuinely good row: `paused: usage limit — retry at 15:10 (28m) · re-dispatch 1/3 · paused 32m`. `chief usage` already reports `limit_incidents` per provider. `chief ps` is `monitor.sh once` and `chief monitor` is `monitor.sh watch` (bin/chief cmd_ps/cmd_monitor), so ONE renderer serves both and a fix lands on both at once.

THREE MEASURED GAPS, all on the path an exhausted account actually takes.

1. DETECTION IS CLAUDE-PHRASED, AND THE DOC SAYS WHAT THAT COSTS. `RATE_LIMIT_PATTERN` / `RATE_LIMIT_STATUS_PATTERN` (engine/agent.sh:571-577) were written against the Claude Code CLI's wordings. `docs/guides/providers.md` §Usage-limit detection states the consequence in its own words: a provider that says it differently "matches nothing, and its limit stop is demoted to a no-progress iteration: the loop burns its budget and exits 1 as a stall, indistinguishable to the driver from a genuinely failed tasklist." The roster is five — `claude`, `devin`, `opencode`, `amp`, `codex` — and four of them have never been verified against that pattern. That is exactly the operator's report: not a display bug, a tasklist that died looking like a failure.

2. A SPENT QUOTA IS RENDERED AS A BAD KEY. `_provider_unavailable` classifies `401 402 403` + `authentication_error` + `permission_error` as one `permanent` bucket and prints one sentence for all of them: "bad or revoked credentials, or a quota that will not replenish". But `402` (and an `insufficient_quota`-shaped error type) means the account is OUT OF CREDIT, which is an operator action — top up — while `401`/`403` mean the credential is wrong. The monitor's own glyph comment (engine/monitor.sh:499-503) says the `no-api` label deliberately does NOT mean "the account is out of quota" — so today nothing anywhere says that sentence.

3. THE REASON IS ON DISK AND THE LIVE SURFACES DO NOT READ IT. `engine/driver.sh:2871` writes the why (`HTTP 402 (…)`) to `$STATE/<name>.unavailable`, and the ONLY reader is the end-of-run summary at `:3745`. In the row renderer, `hold_kind`, `rate-limited`, `paused` and the `awaiting-*` states each get a dedicated note; `provider-unavailable` falls through to the generic phase/agent-note branch (engine/monitor.sh:930-945), so a live row reads `⏸ no-api` + `provider-unavailable for 4m` and never names the HTTP code chief already recorded. An operator watching the run sees less than the summary they get after it ends.

SCOPE AND REFUSALS.
⛔ Do NOT widen `RATE_LIMIT_PATTERN` by guesswork. The pattern is shared and provider-agnostic, and the doc's own warning stands: a pattern that matches ordinary agent prose turns every iteration into a sleep. A phrasing is added only with a recorded observation (provider, CLI version, date, verbatim line) — the same discipline `PROVIDER_TRANSPORT_PATTERN`'s dated list already keeps.
⛔ Do NOT introduce a second ledger. `chief usage` owns incident history; anything this adds is read back out of what the engine already writes.
⛔ Do NOT collapse `rate-limited` and `provider-unavailable`. A window that reopens and an account that needs topping up are different operator actions, and engine/live.sh:78 already forbids conflating them.
⛔ A public repository: name no downstream repo, tasklist or path in code, tests or docs.

ENGINE DISCIPLINE. Editing `engine/`/`bin/` means bumping `VERSION` and README's and ROADMAP's bold version together (test/version-bump.sh, test/doc-sync.sh), and a merged tasklist must be named in ROADMAP.md (scripts/check-roadmap-truth.sh).

userStories.title: A limit no pattern recognises is reported as a suspected limit, not as a stall
acceptanceCriteria: When a worker stops with no progress AND the provider's last output carries a limit-shaped signal that the patterns did not match, the stop is reported as a SUSPECTED usage limit — naming the provider, quoting the line, and saying which pattern would have to be extended — rather than as an ordinary stall. The existing `rate-limited` path is unchanged when a pattern DOES match.

Design the suspicion narrowly and say what it rests on: the provider exited non-zero, nothing was committed, and the output carries a limit-shaped token. State the false-positive cost in the code, as the transport-pattern list already does. A suspected limit must NOT silently start sleeping or re-dispatching — it stops and reports, because acting on a guess is what the pattern discipline exists to prevent.

Both live surfaces show it, through the one renderer: a distinct label and a note saying what chief suspects and what the operator should check. `chief ps` and `chief monitor` are asserted separately in the test, because one is `once` and the other `watch` and only the first is cheap to assert.

A hermetic test in the style of `test/limitstate.sh` (fake provider binary on PATH, behaviour keyed by branch name) covers BOTH directions: a recognised limit still reaches `rate-limited`, and an unrecognised limit-shaped stop reaches the new reporting rather than a bare stall. Add the no-regression case that ordinary agent prose with no limit signal is still an ordinary stall — without it, 'report everything as a suspected limit' passes the suite.
`bash test/all.sh` passes (or the suite's documented subset, named in the notes with what was run), and `VERSION` + README + ROADMAP move together.
userStories.notes: test/suspectlimit.sh (new): PASS — 4 tasklists through the real driver, known-limit -> RATE-LIMITED (unchanged), unknown-limit -> SUSPECTED-LIMIT, and both sabotage controls (non-zero exit with ordinary prose; exit-0 prose ABOUT a quota) still ordinary stalls; `? limit?` + note asserted as a whole line in chief ps AND chief monitor separately. Mutation-checked: before the ${VAR:-} brace fix the same file failed at exactly `want SUSPECTED-LIMIT*`. Ran directly with `bash test/suspectlimit.sh` because a worktree edit to .chief/verify.sh does not run in that branch own gate. Subset run green (not all.sh): doc-sync, version-bump, stall-flag, limitstate, ratelimit, limitmonitor, provider-unavailable, noworkguard, five-cases = 9 passed, 0 failed. quality ratchet: OK, function_length_max +13/tol 15, single_use_functions +2/tol 2. VERSION 0.9.34 -> 0.9.35 with README and ROADMAP bold **v0.9.35**.

userStories.title: Out of credit is its own verdict, separate from a bad credential
acceptanceCriteria: `402`, and an error type that names an exhausted quota, are classified as a distinct permanent kind from `401`/`403`/`authentication_error`/`permission_error`. Both remain permanent — neither is slept on — but they are no longer described by one sentence.

The wording is the operator's next action, not the HTTP fact: an exhausted account says the account has no usage left and what lifts it; a bad credential says the credential is wrong. The classification is read off the provider's own status code or error envelope, never off prose — the rule `docs/reference/provider-unavailability.md` already states.

The distinction reaches the live row label, the run's end-of-run summary block, and the emitted event, so a subscriber can act on it. `docs/reference/provider-unavailability.md`'s permanent table and `docs/reference/status.md` are updated in the same commit; a doc that still shows one bucket is drift the doc-sync gate should catch.

Tests drive a fake provider emitting each of `401`, `402` and `403` and assert three outcomes: all three stop without sleeping, and the two verdicts are distinguishable in what the operator is shown. Sabotage control: collapsing the new kind back into the old one reddens exactly the credit cases and leaves the credential cases green.
`bash test/all.sh` passes, and `VERSION` + README + ROADMAP move together.
userStories.notes: test/provider-credit.sh (new): PASS — all four parts. PART A, three codes through the real agent loop: 402 -> exhausted, 401/403 -> credential, all three exit 8 after exactly ONE provider call with no wait announced and no backoff event; the 529 control on the same knobs was called 3x and waited twice, so 'not slept on' is not vacuous. PART B, staged render: `no-credit` / `bad-key` / `no-api` / `no-api` across four provider-unavailable rows, all four keeping the hold glyph. PART C, real driver: both summary lines name their verdict and the fix, and refusal survives worker_park (exhausted / credential read back off the parked live.json). PART D sabotage: with 402 collapsed back into the credential bucket in a copy of the engine, exactly the credit assertions go red and the credential ones stay green. Subset also green: liveliness, events, provider-unavailable, provider-backoff, limitmonitor, stall-flag, suspectlimit = 7 passed, 0 failed. quality ratchet: OK — function_length_max +13/tol 15, single_use_functions +2/tol 2 (no new function added), mean +0.38/tol 5. doc-sync PASS at v0.9.36; VERSION 0.9.35 -> 0.9.36 with README and ROADMAP bold **v0.9.36**. ALLSH

userStories.title: A held row names who is holding it, using the reason chief already wrote down
acceptanceCriteria: A `provider-unavailable` row in `chief ps` / `chief monitor` gets its own note, beside the existing `limit_note` / `op_note` / `hold_note` family, that reports the recorded reason — the HTTP code and error type chief already writes to `$STATE/<name>.unavailable` and to the live record — plus the retry accounting already carried in `noturn`/`noturn_limit`, and the phase age.

The note reads from what the engine already records; it does not re-derive a reason and does not re-classify. When no reason was recorded, it says the provider refused the request and nothing more — an absent reason must not render as an empty or misleading line.

A permanently-refused row (US-2's two kinds) is visibly distinct from one still retrying a transient refusal, because the operator action differs: one is wait, one is fix the credential, one is top up the account.

`test/limitmonitor.sh` (or a sibling in its style) asserts the rendered row for each case against a staged state directory, so the assertion is about the RENDERER and not about a live provider. Assert one whole output line, not a fragment that the run summary also prints — a needle both surfaces emit cannot tell them apart.
`docs/guides/monitoring.md`'s phase/label tables gain the new rows, and its worked examples show the new notes verbatim, so the documented output matches what the renderer produces.
`bash test/all.sh` passes, `VERSION` + README + ROADMAP move together, and `scripts/check-roadmap-truth.sh` is green.
userStories.notes: test/unavailnote.sh (new): PASS — all three parts. PART A `chief ps` and PART B `chief monitor`, against a staged state dir: four refused rows asserted as WHOLE lines — exhausted (`HTTP 402 (billing_error) · refusal 1/3 · the account has no usage left to spend · PERMANENT … add credit …`), credential (`HTTP 401 (authentication_error) … fix or replace the credential`), transient-spent (`HTTP 503 · refusal 3/3 · each refusal was waited out first …`) and NOTHING recorded (`the provider refused the request · branch + worktree kept · held 4m` — no code, no verdict, no 0/3). The still-retrying control (state running, phase provider-backoff) keeps `provider attempt 2/3` and never says PERMANENT. PART C REPRODUCES: with the new elif neutered in a copy of the engine the same records render `provider-unavailable for 4m` and name no reason; a one-word mutation of the expected note also reddens it. Subset green (see notes on all.sh below): unavailnote, suspectlimit, provider-credit, provider-unavailable, limitmonitor, stall-flag, liveliness = 7 passed, 0 failed; doc-sync PASS at v0.9.37, check-doc-links PASS, scripts/check-roadmap-truth.sh PASS. quality ratchet OK — single_use_functions 59 -> 60 (+1 of tol 2, DOWN from +2: suspect_note and the new note became one two-call-site provider_note), function_length_max +13/tol 15, mean +0.58/tol 5. VERSION 0.9.36 -> 0.9.37 with README and ROADMAP bold **v0.9.37**.
